key_insight: An LLM coding-agent search discovered ELOTE, a shared quantum-simulation protocol that reduced estimated median T-gate cost by 85.35% while retaining chemical accuracy across 115 training Hamiltonians.
engineering_relevance: Jointly optimizing product-formula structure and rotation-synthesis precision can substantially lower estimated fault-tolerant quantum chemistry costs.
method: Run five independent Nemotron 3.5 Lightning coding-agent searches, each with 100 code mutations.
Minimize estimated T-gate cost for 95% success while requiring chemical accuracy on every training Hamiltonian.
Combine identical Pauli strings, use a first-order product formula, and adapt synthesis precision to term properties.
evidence_signal: Classical verification covered 115 training Hamiltonians with 4–16 qubits and 76 larger tests with 18–22 qubits; all met chemical accuracy, while a separately optimized δ-ELOTE reduced geometric-mean cost by another 58.90% versus ELOTE for ten reaction energies.
watch_item: Savings are classically verified cost estimates, not demonstrated quantum-hardware performance; generalization beyond the evaluated Hamiltonians remains unproven.
paper_title: Reducing T gates in product formulas with agent loops
